repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until((#Kitchen_MB).multiButton_button3 != "pushed")
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#Kitchen_MB).multiButton_button3 == "pushed")
(#Kitchen_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(1 SEC)
(#Kitchen_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR implements a rising-edge wait followed by a body. The candidate uses a periodic `if` that only evaluates at the start of the 1-second wrapper period. At t=100ms, the button is pushed, but the candidate's `if` has not yet executed, so the action is missed. The rearming logic is also incorrect because it sets `triggered = true` inside the body, preventing the rising-edge logic from working correctly on subsequent iterations if the condition were to toggle.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` polling pattern with the required rising-edge state machine: block until the condition becomes false (rearm), then block until it becomes true (fire), execute the body, and mark as fired. This ensures the action occurs exactly when the rising edge is detected, regardless of the wrapper period.
